logs_processor #  Description #  Collect the local log files.
Configuration Example #  The elasticsearch log files as an example.
pipeline: - name: log_collect auto_start: true keep_running: true retry_delay_in_ms: 3000 processor: - logs_processor: queue_name: "logs" logs_path: "/opt/es/elasticsearch-7.7.1/logs" # metadata for all log items metadata: category: elasticsearch patterns: - pattern: ".*_server.json$" type: json metadata: name: server timestamp_fields: ["timestamp", "@timestamp"] remove_fields: [ "type", "cluster.name", "cluster.uuid", "node.name", "node.id", "timestamp", "@timestamp", ] - pattern: "gc.log$" type: text metadata: name: gc timestamp_patterns: - "\\d{4}-\\d{1,2}-\\d{1,2}T\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}.\\d{3}\\+\\d{4}" - "\\d{4}-\\d{1,2}-\\d{1,2} \\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2},\\d{3}" - "\\d{4}-\\d{1,2}-\\d{1,2}T\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2},\\d{3}" - pattern: ".*.log$" type: multiline line_pattern: '^\[' metadata: name: server timestamp_patterns: - "\\d{4}-\\d{1,2}-\\d{1,2}T\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}.\\d{3}\\+\\d{4}" - "\\d{4}-\\d{1,2}-\\d{1,2} \\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2},\\d{3}" - "\\d{4}-\\d{1,2}-\\d{1,2}T\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2},\\d{3}" Parameter Description #     Name Type Description     queue_name string Log files collection queue name   logs_path string Log files path   metadata map Configure the metadata for the log files   patterns object Patterns configuration for log files   patterns.pattern string Pattern for log files   patterns.metadata map Configure the metadata for the log files which matched   patterns.type string Log type, support json，text，multiline   patterns.line_pattern string When the log type is multiline, the pattern for a new line   patterns.remove_fields []string Fields that need to be removed (available when the log type is json)   patterns.timestamp_fields []string Timestamp field (available when the log type is json)   patterns.timestamp_patterns []string Timestamp pattern (available when the log type is text and multiline )
title: logs_processor

content:
Authentication #  Login Tokens and API Tokens #  A login Token signs you into the Agent UI.
An API Token calls Agent APIs directly through the X-API-TOKEN header. Each API Token has its own permissions and expiration. Its permissions determine which APIs it can call.
Getting the Login Token #  Automatic Generation and Display #  If you do not configure a login Token, Agent generates one and saves it in the keystore. Agent normally reuses this Token across restarts.
When Agent first generates the login Token, it prints the Token to standard output:
-- Login Token ----------------- | Token: <LOGIN_TOKEN> | ---------------------------------- When Agent restores a Token from the keystore, it hides the Token by default. To display it again, set AGENT_SHOW_LOGIN_TOKEN=1 or true before starting Agent. This variable controls display only. It does not generate a new Token.
macOS or Linux:
AGENT_SHOW_LOGIN_TOKEN=1 ./agent Windows PowerShell:
$env:AGENT_SHOW_LOGIN_TOKEN = "1" .\agent.exe If the keystore cannot save the Token, read the startup warnings. A Token that Agent cannot persist can change after a restart.
Explicit Configuration #  Set the AGENT_LOGIN_TOKEN environment variable or add this top-level section to agent.yml:
security: login_token: "<YOUR_LOGIN_TOKEN>" The environment variable takes precedence over the configuration file. Both take precedence over the saved keystore Token. The current version prints explicitly configured login Tokens at startup.
Creating an API Token #  After logging in to Agent, create an API Token in the UI:
 Open the service management page and click the settings button (gear icon) in the upper-right corner. Select “API Token” from the dropdown menu to open “Token Management”. Click “Add”, enter a name, select the required permissions, and enter an optional description. Then click “Create”. Copy and save the new API Token. After you close the dialog, the management UI cannot display the full Token again. If you lose it, create a new one.  Calling APIs with an API Token #  Send the API Token in the X-API-TOKEN header:
curl http://localhost:23000/elasticsearch/node/_discovery \  -H "X-API-TOKEN: <API_TOKEN>" Protected endpoints return HTTP 401 when authentication fails. They return HTTP 403 when an authenticated API Token lacks the permissions that the endpoint requires.
title: Authentication

Installing the Agent #  INFINI Agent supports mainstream operating systems and platforms. The program package is small, with no extra external dependency. So, the agent can be installed very rapidly
Downloading #  Automatic install
curl -sSL http://get.infini.cloud | bash -s -- -p agent  The above script can automatically download the latest version of the corresponding platform’s agent and extract it to /opt/agent
  The optional parameters for the script are as follows:
   -v [version number]（Default to use the latest version number）
   -d [installation directory] (default installation to /opt/agent)
 Manual install
Select a package for downloading in the following URL based on your operating system and platform:
 https://release.infinilabs.com/agent/
System Service #  To run the data platform of INFINI Agent as a background task, run the following commands:
➜ ./agent -service install Success ➜ ./agent -service start Success Unloading the service is simple. To unload the service, run the following commands:
➜ ./agent -service stop Success ➜ ./agent -service uninstall Success
title: Installing the Agent
